approach: Three changes meeting in the throughput review. (1) athena-data: a `WasteFigures` struct (attempts per landing, wasted USD, first-attempt share), a defaulted optional `waste` field on `ThroughputReview`, and a `Wasted` trigger; old records still parse. (2) status.rs: `waste_windows(records, window)` measures the three figures over the newest 20 landings and the 3 windows of 20 before them; `Throughput::compute` stores the newest window (`waste`), the one before it (`waste_previous`), the same two for the median (`median_previous`), and the noise for each measure. `Throughput::text()` prints the three measures, each with a basis line; `athena status` and `status --snapshot` already print `text()` (display.rs:1114, :1203), so display.rs and snapshot.rs are not edited. (3) hestia.rs: `throughput_due` gains the current figures and fires `Wasted` on a rise of more than 20% against the figures stored on the previous review (the existing stored-baseline pattern, which stops repeated firing). `throughput_review` no longer skips because a design request is open: it notes the open request in the record and names it in THROUGHPUT.md. A pure `request_gate` decides whether to ask the model and queue a request, from ONE like-for-like comparison: the newest 20-landing window against the 20 before it, for the median and each of the three measures, against the noise = the largest adjacent difference among the OLDER non-overlapping windows (window 1 vs 2, 2 vs 3). The note says "within noise", "no measure worsened", "no earlier window / noise not estimated", or names the measures that exceeded noise. The 25% slowdown rule and the stage-growth comparison are unchanged. No parser, stem list or reading rule changes, so refusal_corpus is not touched.

decisions.choice: Definitions. Attempt = a request job that did work (has invocations) or a landed job. Landing = a landed request job. First-attempt landing = a landed job whose request is not 'try again on <job>' pointing at an earlier job that did work (`reading::retried_job`, the link `planning_cost` uses). Wasted spend = `JobRecords::spent_usd` (store.rs:169) summed over attempts that did not land, using the same 'did not land' predicate as `unlanded_jobs` (status.rs:1015-1018), moved into a shared helper `did_not_land(job)`.
decisions.reason: All figures come from job and invocation records, so no new record type is needed. spent_usd also counts jobs stopped before an outcome carries totals. The retry link is the codebase's existing meaning of 'another attempt at the same change'.

rejected.why: Jobs stopped before an outcome carry no totals.

rejected.option: Count attempts as invocations or producer runs
rejected.why: A job's planner, critic and verifier runs are not attempts to land a change; the request's '58% of attempts did not land' is about jobs.

decisions.choice: Windows. Rank all landed request jobs by (landing end, id), the order `landed_jobs_among_first` uses (status.rs:963). Window 0 = the newest 20 landings plus every unlanded attempt that ended at or after the 20th-newest landing's end. Window 1 = landings 21-40 plus unlanded attempts that ended between the 40th and 20th cut times; windows 2 and 3 likewise. A window is reported only when it holds 20 landings. `waste_windows(records, window)` takes the size so tests can use small windows; production passes THROUGHPUT_WINDOW. The median uses the same cut over measured landed jobs (`landed_jobs`).
decisions.reason: Matches 'newest 20 landings and the 20 before' with no second time axis. A thin window cannot trigger or gate anything.

rejected.why: Landings per day vary, so a window would not be 20 changes.

rejected.option: Only the measured landed jobs of landed_jobs() for the waste figures
rejected.why: It drops landed jobs that ran no model, which are still landings and attempts. (The median keeps them out, as today.)

decisions.choice: Trigger (`throughput_due`) compares the current newest-window figures with the figures stored on the previous review (new `waste: Option<WasteFigures>`), exactly as the median trigger uses `window_median_minutes`, and needs a landing since that review. Rises: attempts per landing > previous x WORSEN_RATIO; wasted USD > previous x WORSEN_RATIO; first-attempt share < previous x (2 - WORSEN_RATIO). Floor for a rise from zero (finding 7): when the previous wasted USD is 0, a wasted-spend rise counts only if attempts per landing also exceeds previous x WORSEN_RATIO, i.e. more than one unlanded attempt per five landings, not one failed run. A previous review with no stored figures gives no waste trigger. The note on the record says when a rise started from zero.
decisions.reason: A level that stays high triggers once, not on every landing, and old records stay valid. The zero floor ties 'a rise' to a measured quantity (the ratio already used for attempts) instead of a fixed 0.01 USD.

rejected.option: Trigger on newest 20 vs the 20 before, recomputed from records
rejected.why: A level that stays high would fire on every new landing, since the window shifts by one each time.

rejected.option: Any wasted spend of 0.01 USD or more after a zero baseline
rejected.why: One failed run after a clean window would fire a review.
One `Wasted` variant suffices; the note names the measures that rose.

decisions.choice: The request gate (`request_gate`) measures the change as window 0 against window 1 (`waste` vs `waste_previous`; median vs `median_previous`), NOT against the stored review figures, and measures noise as the largest adjacent difference among the older non-overlapping windows (|w1-w2|, and |w2-w3| when window 3 is full), per measure, in that measure's own unit (minutes, attempts, USD, share). A measure counts only when it moved in the bad direction (median, attempts, spend up; share down) by MORE than its noise (equal is within noise). Needs windows 0, 1 and 2 full (60 landings) for noise; with window 1 absent (under 40 landings) the change cannot be judged, and with noise absent any worsening is judged against zero. Both cases queue and the note says which. The first review (no previous review) always asks. The note and hestia.md state this basis.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2: change and noise are now both non-overlapping 20-landing differences, so they are like for like. It excludes the newest pair from its own noise and matches the request's 'larger than the noise between recent windows'. The trigger keeps the stored baseline, which only decides when a review runs.

rejected.option: Change = current vs the previous review's stored figures
rejected.why: That review may be 1 to 9 landings old, so its window shares 11 to 19 landings with window 0 and the change is diluted against a full non-overlapping noise.

rejected.option: Noise measured at the same lag as the stored baseline
rejected.why: Needs a lag that varies per review and per-landing series for spend and share.

rejected.option: Standard error inside the two windows
rejected.why: Not 'noise between recent windows' as accepted, and needs per-job series.
It is the 20% trigger again and does not adapt to the repository.

decisions.choice: An open design request no longer stops the review. The record's note says 'throughput design request <id> is still open; this review ran anyway', THROUGHPUT.md names the open request so the model proposes a different change, and a new design request is queued only if the gate says the change is beyond noise (or noise/baseline cannot be judged). When the gate rejects, no model is asked, so the review costs nothing.
decisions.reason: This is 'does not skip a run' plus 'notes the open request'. The gate is what 'only queues when larger than the noise' needs.

rejected.option: Keep the skip and reword it
rejected.why: The request calls the skipped runs 'did nothing'; today's code already writes a record and skips the model (hestia.rs:1728-1733).

rejected.option: Ask the model but never queue while a request is open
rejected.why: The proposal would be recorded and acted on by nobody.

decisions.choice: Effect on `improvement_of` and the guaranteed turn. Two open design requests are now possible. `improvement_of` (hestia.rs:409-443) returns a set of every waiting `proposal.request_job`, and `Plan::build_improving` (plan.rs:832-839) treats `improvement.items` as a set (`improving` closure), so both requests get the guaranteed turn (main.rs:288 help text). The plan tests this at the hestia level (the criterion 3 test asserts both ids appear) and relies on the set-based plan tests (plan.rs ~1952-2002) for the dispatch order. The existing test `improvement_of_lists_the_throughput_design_request_and_not_the_slowdown_request` (hestia.rs:5116) has its second half rewritten.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. After the change the second half's review (21 landings, so no earlier window) queues a design request, so `items` is no longer empty; the rewrite still isolates the slowdown request by asserting items equals exactly the new design request, holds neither the slowdown job nor the unlinked earlier request job.

rejected.option: Leave the test and say it passes unchanged
rejected.why: It would fail: items holds the new design request.

rejected.option: Queue nothing while a design request is open
rejected.why: Contradicts the request's 'does not skip a run'.

risks.risk: The gate makes reviews that see no worsening ask no model and queue nothing, a behaviour change beyond the trigger wording, and may read to the user like a run that did nothing.
risks.mitigation: The record's note states why in each case ('within noise', 'no measure worsened'), the first review always asks, and the CHANGELOG and hestia.md state it. Open question 2 asks the user.

risks.risk: With under 60 landings the noise cannot be estimated, so any worsening queues a request.
risks.mitigation: The note says the noise was not estimated and how many landings it needs; this is not worse than today, where every review asked.

risks.risk: Two design requests can be open at once, and both receive the guaranteed turn.
risks.mitigation: A second is queued only beyond noise; THROUGHPUT.md names the open request so the proposal differs; the criterion 3 test and the rewritten improvement_of test assert the set; build_improving is set-based.

risks.risk: Existing hestia tests assert the model is not called while a request is open (~4628, ~4724, ~4790) and the improvement_of test at 5116 assumes no new design request.
risks.mitigation: Step 6 lists and rewrites each; the slowdown assertions stay so the unchanged 25% rule is still covered.

risks.risk: Window and retry reconstruction can drift: a landing record written later moves the landing end, and a 'try again on' link can point at a missing job.
risks.mitigation: A missing or unrun predecessor counts as no predecessor; the doc says the figures are a reconstruction, as `previous_stage_medians` does.

risks.risk: A new record field makes a newer record unreadable by an older Athena because of deny_unknown_fields.
risks.mitigation: skip_serializing_if keeps the field out until the new code writes it; forward reading by old binaries is already limited for every new field in the crate.

risks.risk: Failed-job fixtures end in the wrong window, so the criterion 2(b) and 4(b) figures are off.
risks.mitigation: seed_failed starts each job 30 minutes after its slot's landing start with a 5-minute producer; landings end 20 minutes after their start and the next starts 2 hours later (hestia.rs:4281-4283), and the test asserts `waste_windows` counts per window before asserting the review.

demonstrations.method: Two tests. (a) Pure `request_gate`: change of 0.1 attempts per landing against noise 0.3 gives queue=false and a note containing 'within noise'; change 0.5 against 0.3 gives queue=true and a note naming the measure, the change and the noise; change exactly equal to the noise is within noise; noise None with any worsening gives queue=true and a note saying the noise was not estimated; window 1 absent gives queue=true and a note saying there is no earlier window; no worsening gives queue=false with 'no measure worsened'.
